title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 240 (Liability of officers in respect of offences committed prior to merger, amalgamation, etc.)

content.overview: Section 240 provides that notwithstanding anything in any other law for the time being in force, the liability in respect of offences committed under this Act by the officers in default of the transferor company prior to its merger, amalgamation or acquisition shall continue after such merger, amalgamation or acquisition.
content.glance: Officers in default of the transferor company remain liable for offences under the Act committed before the merger, amalgamation or acquisition; the scheme does not extinguish that personal liability.
content.study: Notwithstanding anything in any other law for the time being in force, the liability in respect of offences committed under this Act by the officers in default, of the transferor company prior to its merger, amalgamation or acquisition shall continue after such merger, amalgamation or acquisition. Current-law framing: identify an offence under the Act by an officer in default of the transferor company before the appointed date of the merger, amalgamation or acquisition; apply the rule that liability continues after the scheme; the successor company is not a shield for past officers. The section preserves existing liability; it does not create a new offence.

sections.heading: Continuing Liability
sections.body: Liability of officers in default of the transferor company for offences under the Act committed before merger, amalgamation or acquisition continues after the scheme takes effect.

sections.heading: Notwithstanding Clause
sections.body: The rule applies notwithstanding anything in any other law for the time being in force.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Applies to merger, amalgamation or acquisition under the Chapter; preserves personal liability of officers in default; does not create a new offence.

provisions.title: Liability of officers in respect of offences committed prior to merger, amalgamation, etc.

examples.title: Pre-merger offence survives
examples.body: A director of the transferor company commits an offence under the Act six months before the amalgamation appointed date. After amalgamation, prosecution may continue against that director under s. 240; the scheme does not wipe the liability.

examples.title: Not a new offence
examples.body: Section 240 does not invent a fresh offence for the post-merger period. It keeps alive liability for offences already committed under the Act by officers in default of the transferor before the scheme.

hypotheticals.question: Does amalgamation under s. 232 automatically discharge officers of the transferor from past Act offences?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 240 expressly provides that liability in respect of offences committed under the Act by officers in default of the transferor company prior to merger, amalgamation or acquisition shall continue after such merger, amalgamation or acquisition.

distinctions.title: Continuing officer liability (s. 240) vs merger/amalgamation (s. 232)
distinctions.left: Personal liability of transferor officers for pre-scheme Act offences continues
distinctions.right: Transfer of property and liabilities of the company; dissolution without winding up

misconceptions.trap: Once the transferor is dissolved without winding up, its officers cannot be prosecuted for pre-merger Act offences.
misconceptions.correction: Section 240 provides that liability of officers in default for offences under the Act committed prior to the merger, amalgamation or acquisition continues after the scheme. Dissolution of the company does not extinguish that personal liability.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 240 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify pre-scheme Act offence by transferor officer in default. II. Apply continuing-liability rule. III. Note scheme does not extinguish personal liability. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Offence facts and date; officer status; scheme timing; precise relief.

examTips: Pre-merger Act offences of transferor officers survive the scheme.
Does not create a new offence — preserves existing liability.
